# PROTOCOL.md — FIGO-KI-XF Frozen Protocol (v1.0)

**Status: FROZEN as of 2026-08-18.** Do not edit after Phase 1 begins. Any
later change gets a new version number (v1.1, v1.2, ...) appended below and
forces re-run of all prior result rows under the new version. This document
is the single artifact that protects every reported number in this project
from the reviewer question "did you tune the protocol until you hit 0.86?"

Source: `FIGO-KI-Crossformer_Project_Plan.md` (Phase 0, section 0.1).

---

## 1. The Seven Frozen Decisions

| # | Decision | Frozen setting | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Positive label** | Umbilical artery pH ≤ 7.05 | Standard severe-acidaemia cut in CTU-CHB literature. |
| 2 | **Secondary label** (reported, never tuned on) | BDecf > 12 mmol/L | Sensitivity analysis only, reported once at the end. |
| 3 | **Signal window** | Final 30 minutes before delivery, last-aligned | Matches the deployable decision-support use case. |
| 4 | **Stage-II handling** | Include. Log stage-II fraction per record as a covariate for subgroup analysis. | Excluding it inflates AUC and is a known source of cross-paper incomparability. |
| 5 | **Resampling** | 4 Hz native → 1 Hz model input (7200 → 1800 timesteps over the 30-min window) | Keeps FIGO-relevant morphology; makes segment-wise attention tractable. |
| 6 | **Channels** | FHR + UC (2 variates) + missingness mask (3rd auxiliary channel, not attended over as a "variate" by cross-dimension attention) | Crossformer's cross-dimension attention is only meaningful with ≥2 real variates. |
| 7 | **Cross-validation** | 5×5 nested, stratified by primary label, grouped by record ID | No record may appear in both train and test at any level. |

## 2. Exclusion Cascade

Applied in this fixed order, exactly as specified by the source plan
(section 0.1). N logged at every step.

1. Missing pH **or** missing BDecf → drop (both must be present, even
   though BDecf only feeds the secondary sensitivity analysis — this is
   the plan's literal rule, kept as-is rather than relaxed, since the
   expected-surviving-N range of 430–480 was calibrated against it).
2. Records where the final 30 min contains > 50% signal loss (FHR == 0,
   assessed pre-interpolation — i.e. on the raw native-rate gap mask
   before any PCHIP fill) → drop.
3. Records with < 20 min of usable trace after gap handling (i.e. after
   the full section-3 gap/artifact chain, on whatever trace remains once
   truncated to the final 30 min) → drop.

Expected surviving N: roughly 430–480 of 552 (per plan). The exact cascade
table (N remaining after each step) is generated by
`scripts/run_exclusion_cascade.py` and reported in
`docs/exclusion_cascade_report.md`. A deviation of more than ~10% from the
plan's expected range must be reported explicitly, not silently absorbed.

## 3. Preprocessing Pipeline (fixed, shared by every experiment)

```
raw FHR (4 Hz)
  -> clip to physiological range [50, 200] bpm; values outside -> marked as gap
  -> gap detection: contiguous runs of zeros/out-of-range
  -> gaps <= 15 s: Hermite (PCHIP) spline interpolation
  -> gaps > 15 s: leave as gap, carry a binary missingness mask forward
  -> artifact removal: reject samples where |FHR[t] - FHR[t-1]| > 25 bpm
                        (stable-segment rule; re-interpolate)
  -> downsample to 1 Hz by 4-sample median
  -> per-record z-normalisation of FHR using TRAIN-FOLD statistics only
```

The missingness mask is a third input channel to the model (and an input to
the FIGO extractor) — never silently interpolated away.

UC channel: clip to [0, 100] TOCO units, same gap logic, no z-normalisation
(per-record min-max; relative amplitude is informative).

**Interpretive note (does not change the seven frozen decisions, just
resolves ambiguous phrasing from the source plan before implementation):**
- *FHR normalisation* ("per-record z-normalisation ... using train-fold
  statistics only") is implemented as **per-channel z-normalisation, fit by
  pooling all training-fold records together**, mirroring standard ML
  hygiene (fit on train, apply to val/test) — a literal single-record
  self-z-score would erase real amplitude differences between records
  (e.g. a persistently low baseline), which the pipeline needs to keep.
- *UC normalisation* ("per-record min-max on the train fold") is implemented
  as **genuine per-record (self-referential) min-max** — each record
  normalised by its own signal's min/max after gap-filling. This is
  fold-independent by construction (no leakage possible) and matches the
  real-world justification given (TOCO transducer belt tension/calibration
  varies per attachment, so relative-within-record amplitude is what's
  informative, not cross-record comparability).

## 4. Baseline Reproduction Gate (Phase 0 exit criterion)

CTG-Crossformer (dimension-segment-wise embedding, two-stage attention,
hierarchical encoder) reproduced AUROC must land within ±0.03 of the
published 0.822 over 10 seeds, **or** a written diagnosis of why not is
recorded in `docs/baseline_reproduction_report.md`, with the reproduced
number adopted as the true baseline for everything downstream. Phase 1 does
not start until this gate closes.

Three trivial baselines are also run once and never revisited during
tuning: logistic regression on classical CTG features, 1D-ResNet on raw
FHR+UC, gradient-boosted trees on classical features.

## 5. Target

AUROC ≥ 0.86 (mean over ≥10 seeds), lower bound of the 95% CI above the
reproduced baseline mean.

## 6. Change Log

- **v1.0 (2026-08-18)**: Initial freeze. All seven decisions and the
  exclusion cascade set as above.
